sections.heading: Raids: raid nights
sections.lead: See a team's raid nights before you join it.
lines: Teams can say which nights they raid: see when you're expected before you join.
Every team banner shows its week, the raid nights lit gold, and the hours under it.
A hollow gold day is an optional night: come if you can.
Hover the nights for each night's hours and the team's note.
Times show in your own clock, and stay put when the clocks change.

lines.text: Organizers: click Raid nights on the team's banner (or ··· > Raid nights) to set them.
Pick the days, set each night's hours, mark optional nights and add a note.

lines: The waitlist shows the nights above Join, so you know what you sign up for.

sections.heading: Welcome tour
sections.lead: A short tour of the addon, made for the roles you hold.
lines: New: a Welcome tour on the real window, one part for each role you hold.
Everyone gets the basics: raids, answers, your BiS list, loot, where things are.
Raid leaders, officers, the guild council and the Guild Master each get their own part.
It asks once, the first time you open the window. Not now means it never asks again.
Untick the parts you don't want. The bar at the bottom jumps between parts.
Exit any time: Settings > Tutorials goes on from the step you stopped at.
The council part runs on demo data, so every view has something in it. Nothing is sent.
Got a new role? Only that part is offered, once (turn it off in Settings > Tutorials).
Settings > Tutorials: every part, the strategy board's tutorial, a look at other roles.

lines.text: Guild Master: a Set up your guild checklist, in Settings > Tutorials and on Home.

lines: /dz tour starts it too.

sections.heading: Raids: hide a raid you won't go to
lines: Another team's raid in your way? ··· > Hide from my board (or right-click the card).
A weekly raid hides for one week or every week. Only you stop seeing it.
Hidden raids leave Upcoming, the Home banner and the reminders.
Changed your mind? The time filter's Hidden view shows them again.

sections.heading: Raids: attendance counts the time you were there
sections.lead: Counts the time you were there, not just if you came.
lines: Attendance is the share of the expected time you were there, not just whether you came.
A team raid expects its own lineup: a 10-man player is never missing from the 25.
A raid without a team expects whoever answered Accept. Pugs and guests are never counted.
Short disconnects don't count, and a few minutes late still counts as on time.

lines.text: The Guild Master sets those minutes in Settings > Attendance. Everyone can see them there.

lines: Came on your alt? It counts for you: your characters are one player.

lines.text: Raid log > Raids > Attendance: a time bar per player, boss kills marked.
Raid log > Attendance: everyone's last raids, late, left early, no-shows and the %.

lines: Click a player for their page: every raid, the last 12 at a glance.
Left early or gave a reason? It goes to Reviews and doesn't count until decided.

lines.text: The Guild Master, officers and guild council decide: Excuse or Counts, with a note.
Pick the reason straight from what they said in chat or a whisper. Tick several lines.
Away for a week? Officers excuse every raid of those days in one go.

lines: A fill-in for a player who left is never counted late, and their help shows.

lines.text: Raid leaders: when someone leaves, swap someone in, bench them or ask the officers.

lines: Left a raid early yourself? Tell the officers why in a few clicks.
Your own attendance is on your Members card (Attendance tab).

lines.text: Officers now see the Raid log's attendance. Loot handed out stays with the loot council.

lines: Raid log: a Gruul + Mag night shows both raids' art and names, and counts every boss.

sections.heading: Raids: loot rules for prized items
sections.lead: A few drops (DST, Warglaives, Thori'dal) have stricter rules, shown to all.
lines: New Raids > Loot rules: the few drops with stricter rules (DST, Warglaives, Thori'dal).
Everyone sees each item's rules and how they stand: You qualify, Free 25 Oct, #1 in queue.
Rules: attendance, rank, mains only, guild only, a cooldown, spec order, a queue, a pair.
Also: only players with it on their BiS list, and how many of the council must agree.
Each rule is Required (keeps you out) or Priority (who meets it goes first).

lines.text: The Guild Master and the guild council add items and edit the rules in place.
Start a new item from a template: Legendary, Top trinket, or another item's rules.

lines: Two items can share one set of rules: the Warglaives go to the same player.
Every change tells the guild what changed and stays in the item's History.

lines.text: On the drop panel, a player who breaks a rule shows the rule and is never suggested.
The council decides prized items: the award needs its votes from the council in the raid.
Giving it against a rule asks why; the reason shows in the loot log and the History.

lines: Your roll pop-up says if you meet the rules; if not, why and when you can again.
Item tooltips say in one line if you qualify for a prized item, or which rule you miss.
Qualify today: hover the icons or the count for names. Next in line: priority rules only.

sections.heading: What's new, easier to read
sections.lead: Highlights first, one line per section, Show me.
lines: The Changelog reads in three layers: highlight cards, one line per section, the lines.
Click a section to open it. Show me opens the page it is about and points at what changed.
Missed a few versions? Since your last visit merges them into one page.
Just for me folds away what is only for the loot council, officers or other classes.
Chips filter by area (Raids, Loot, Gear...); the search finds a word in every version.
From your feedback: everything you asked for that shipped, next to your own words.
Home's What's new chip opens a short pop-up of the highlights.
Tick Open by itself after an update to get that pop-up once per new version.

sections.heading: Themes for the Blessings and Totem bars
lines: Pick a look for your class tool bars: Halo, Sigil, Slate, Gilded or Pips.
Settings > Class tools > Blessings or Totems > Theme. Point at one to try it on your bar.
One theme for all your characters: your paladin's and your shaman's bars match.
The column and the row now look exactly alike: the same buttons, sizes and spacing.
The column shows each blessing with the class in its corner, like the row did.
Your aura, Righteous Fury, Symbols, Heroism and Mana Tide come first, then a thin line.
What to do next lifts out of the bar toward its note: up in the row, left in the column.
The bar's first button opens its planner. It never casts anything.
Symbols of Kings only shows your count now: open the planner with the first button.
Pin your class's planner to the minimap button: + on the arc, then Blessings or Totems.

sections.heading: Themes for the meters
lines: Pick a look for your damage and threat meters: Flat, Halo, Sigil, Slate, Gilded or Pips.
Settings > Meters > Look > Theme. Point at a theme to try it on your panels.
Bar colour by class, by role or one colour for all.
Icons by spec, by class or none; compact or roomy rows; how much background shows.
Numbers as 380.1k, 380,112 or 380k.

sections.heading: Shorter item tooltips
sections.lead: One short line per topic, marked with the DZ seal. Hold Shift for everything.
lines: The addon adds a few short lines to item tooltips now, each marked with the small DZ seal.
Your BiS line names every phase at once: Your BiS P1–P4 · Trinket 1.
Loot council: who wants it fits on one line, players in the raid first.
Hold Shift for everything: each prized rule ticked, every player with what they wear now.
Shift works on a tooltip that is already open too. Comparison tooltips stay short.

sections.heading: Loot council: who is on a dry streak
lines: When loot drops, each player shows how many raids they came to since their last item.
The bars warm up from grey to gold, orange and red: the driest players stand out.
Hover a player for the item they got last, how many days ago and the bosses since.
An item on any of their characters counts. Offspec, disenchant and bank loot don't.
Raids they were benched for or skipped don't count, and neither does tonight's.
Only the guild council sees it: they hold the whole Loot Log.
Only gear ends a streak: a bag, a pattern, a formula or a mount doesn't.
Tier tokens and Magtheridon's Head still count: they turn into gear.
"Won N" and the items in the Raid log and the Guest book leave non-gear out too.
Fixed: hovering a player on the boss drop panel could throw a Lua error.

sections.heading: Raids > Loot rules, for everyone
sections.lead: How the winner is picked, and where you stand.
lines: Every member can read the guild's loot rules now: Raids > Loot rules, or /dz lootrules.
How it's decided: four steps on a gold path, from who can be suggested to the roll.
The steps follow the Guild Master's choices: the floor, a split vote, longest use.
Where you stand: your attendance, your BiS list, longest use and the prized items.
Prized items: a card for each, with your standing; open one for its rules and history.
Read only: the Guild Master changes the rules in Council > Rules.
A two-hander in your main hand leaves the off hand out of your BiS count, as in My BiS.

sections.heading: Loot council: Council > Rules, how the winner is picked
lines: Council > Rules gathers the guild's loot rules: how the winner is picked and prized items.
A split vote (a tie for the most votes) goes to the highest roll among them.
Whoever didn't roll never wins a split. Or the Guild Master lets the council pick.
Attendance floor: under it a player is listed with a warning but never suggested.
Before anyone votes: BiS lists first or the roll only; then the roll or the driest.
Since loot counts only raids someone was really there for (a kill or half the night).
Try it: an example roll re-ranks as you change the rules and says why.
Longest use: who keeps the item on their BiS list for more phases goes first in a list.
It counts up to P3, P4 or P5: with P4, swapping it out in P5 counts as keeping it.
Longest use and the dry streak are separate: both on, longest use first, then the driest.
A class that can't use the item sits with the passes, greyed: never suggested, no votes.
Rules has two pages, Picking the winner and Prized items, each with the whole width.
Picking the winner: a raid banner with Save & share, choices that glide, rows that slide.
Only the Guild Master changes them; Save & share sends them to the whole guild.
Prized items are set up there too.
The drop panel marks a split vote and shows who is under the attendance floor.
The Council's Drops button is gone: /dz drops and Shift-click the minimap button.
A prized item's tooltip, anywhere in the game, wears an orange PRIZED ITEM ribbon.
On the boss drop panel a prized item's card glows amber, soft sheens gliding on its edges.
Settings > Demo mode > Demo a roll rolls a prized item; in demo mode you meet its rules.
A prized item being rolled shows the council's votes against how many must agree.
A prized item's roll window wears the ribbon and glow, with a flash as it opens.
Demo a roll is a menu: a random prized drop or a scenario for each loot rule.
Scenarios: split vote, popular but absent, dry streak, longest use, wrong class, more.
Each one says in chat what to look at and which Council > Rules choice changes it.
Also from chat: /dz demo list, then /dz demo <name> (for example /dz demo split).
Pressing Roll throws a die: it tumbles, the numbers flicker, your roll lands with a glow.
A prized item's Award stays grey until it's allowed: a pip for each council vote it needs.
Its right-click Award says why it isn't allowed yet (a broken rule, votes still missing).
Clicking it anyway asks for a reason: the award goes through and everyone sees why.
A rolled prized item you don't qualify for: no roll window, a short notice says why.
The Guild Master can show the roll window anyway: Council > Rules, Prized: not qualified.

sections.heading: Loot council: a tidier roll list
lines: The boss drop's list runs the card's full width: nothing is cut off any more.
Votes sit in a square at the start of each row: the count, gold when yours is in.
Click the square to vote for that player, click again to take your vote back.
Each player's attendance % has its own column: green from 90%, amber under 75%.
Specs show the way raiders say them (Prot, Resto, MM); hover a player for the full name.
A second roll shows as x2 after the first one, which counts. A bad range shows in red.
Small titles name the columns (Vote, Att, Since loot, Roll), with faint lines between.

sections.heading: One look everywhere
sections.lead: The addon's own dialogs instead of the game's red ones.
lines: Questions and confirmations are the addon's own dialogs now, not the game's red ones.
They open over the window they belong to, with a title, and Escape closes them.
Deleting something has a red button, so it never looks like the safe choice.
Panels, the raid reminder and the strategy prompts lost their rounded game borders.

sections.heading: Paladins: blessings strip
lines: The strip bar's blessings are round, with a ring around each that drains as it runs out.
The ring turns red when a blessing runs short and gold on the one to do next.
The class sits on the top-right corner, the red count of who is missing it top-left.
No more "5 missing" chip: the red count says it. The chip only shows the time left.

sections.heading: Swing timer: twist practice
lines: Learn twisting step by step: Practice on the swing timer's card or /dz swing practice.
Five short lessons, each adding one thing: twist, Command, Strike, Judgement, Bloodlust.
You press your own keys, read from your action bars. Nothing is cast, no target needed.
Your latency is added, so the timing you learn is the timing of a real fight.
A coach over the ring says what to press next, with your key on it.
After each swing: Perfect, Twist, Early 62 ms, Late, Missed or Blocked by a cooldown.
The ruler under the ring shows where each Seal of Blood landed against the window.
Up to 3 stars per lesson, scored against a perfect run on the same swings.
A star opens the next lesson. Free play runs the full rotation as long as you like.
Alliance paladins see Seal of the Martyr everywhere, not Seal of Blood.
The ring's colors now meet in flat edges, and the fill ends in a flat line.

sections.heading: My BiS: Epic, Rare or Uncommon gems
sections.lead: Pick the gem quality the fill suggests for your list.

lines.text: Suggest > Gems and enchants: pick Epic, Rare or Uncommon gems for your list.

lines: The fill finds the strongest gems of that quality; your meta gem keeps its colours.
The gem editor has an Epic | Rare | Uncommon switch: the choices show that quality's gems.

sections.heading: Lighter on memory
lines: Every event and addon message makes less garbage, so DisasterZone's memory climbs slower.
With the threat meter on, meters don't redraw five times a second when nothing changed.
The swing timer shown out of combat no longer repaints its ring every frame.
Settings > About: a Performance page shows DisasterZone's memory and CPU (off by default).

sections.heading: Gear sim: recent runs
sections.lead: Your last 10 runs are kept: open one again, or compare two.
lines: The gear sim keeps your last 10 runs on each character, also after a /reload.
Sets you simmed before aren't simmed again: a rerun of the same gear is instant.
A saved set checks its first fights first, so an update never shows old numbers.
Recent runs (under the result): click a run to see it, or two to compare them.
Compare shows the DPS on the same rolls, the gear between them and any other settings.
Open brings a run back: its Working set, settings and result, with nothing to sim.
Compare with: pick an earlier run's Working set to sim against.
Nerd stats and Recent runs now sit on the window's own background.

sections.heading: Gear sim: gems and enchants
lines: Change the gems and enchant of any Working set slot: click its gem strip.
Or right-click the slot > Gems and enchant. Use suggested fills the spec's picks.
A slot with other gems shows as Changed, and the next run sims them.
Your My BiS list's gems stay as they are.

sections.heading: Fixes
lines: Officers no longer send each other the raid blacklist every few seconds (less lag).
The paladin buff bar redraws only when something changes, not every second (less lag).
In a fight the buff bar's timers and missing counts keep up instead of freezing.
Options > AddOns > DisasterZone fits again: smaller cards, every page on one screen.

changelog.title: Raid nights, loot rules for everyone and a Welcome tour

sections.heading: Damage and threat meters
sections.lead: Built-in damage and threat meters, opt-in.
lines: Built-in meters: no need for Details or a threat addon. Off until you turn them on.
Turn them on in Settings > Meters, or with /dz meter on and /dz threat on.
Damage, DPS, healing, damage taken, deaths, interrupts, dispels and active time.
Numbers match Details: the whole hit counts, and DPS is by each player's active time.
Threat comes from the game itself: the gold line marks where you pull aggro.
Near your pull point your bar turns red, the screen edges flash and a sound plays.
Tanks see how close everyone is to pulling, closest first.
Everything is a panel: + on a header adds one, x closes it, any panel shows any view.
Unlocked, drag a panel under another to dock it, or onto its header to make a tab.
Panels are as tall as their rows; drag the corner to set the width and the row count.
Hover a bar for top abilities. Click it for a full breakdown, or a death recap.
Your own bar stays in view, and melee shows your weapon's icon.
Nothing is shared or posted: each player counts their own combat log.

sections.heading: Gear sim
sections.lead: What a gear change is worth, in real DPS.
lines: New Gear sim page (Gear menu): sim your gear and see what a change is worth, in real DPS.
It plays the fight out a thousand times with WoWSims' rotation, buffs and numbers.
The doll becomes your Working set: it starts as the gear you wear.
Click a slot for the item picker (your gear and bags first); picks go to the Working set.
Best for this slot sims what the picker lists (filters and search narrow it) and ranks it.
Click the round sigil to sim the Working set against your gear or a BiS phase, same luck.
You see the DPS change, how sure it is, and a verdict in plain words.
While it runs, the ticks light up and the average settles live under a running line.
The settings read as one sentence: click an underlined word to change it.
Fights: Quick (300), Normal (1,000) or Precise (3,000).
Changed slots are marked gold. It pauses in combat and only runs when you click.
Nerd stats: DPS per fight, every ability, swing outcomes, buff uptimes, mana, the run.
Stat weights on demand: one paired sim per stat, for your Working set.
A set it has simmed before is not simmed again: change one slot and only that set runs.
Fury and Arms Warriors can sim too, with WoWSims' Warrior rotations and raid setup.
Enhancement Shamans too: twisted totems, Stormstrike, shocks and the Fire Elemental.
Rogues too: Combat, Mutilate and Hemorrhage builds, poisons and their own Expose Armor.
Feral Druids too, in cat form: powershifting, Shred, Rip, Mangle and Ferocious Bite.
Elemental Shamans too: Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning with overloads and totems.
Shadow Priests too: Mind Flay clipped as in WoWSims, Vampiric Touch and the Shadowfiend.
Balance Druids too: Starfire (downranked on low mana), Moonfire and Force of Nature.
Mages too: Arcane, Fire and Frost, with mana gems, Evocation, Ignite and Water Elemental.
Warlocks too: all three specs, with your curse, Life Tap and your demon or its sacrifice.
Hunters too: Auto Shot, Steady Shot, Kill Command and your pet, with its focus.
More item effects count: Thunderfury, Blinkstrike, The Night Blade, Rod of the Sun King...
Swapped-in items get gems that keep your meta gem on; the card warns when a meta is off.
The ... menu copies the exact sim input for WoWSims (Import > JSON), to compare both sims.
Build your own buff presets: New preset in the buffs list, then click buffs on or off.
Your presets are saved for all your characters; edit or delete them from the same list.
Each team lineup you are on shows in the buffs list and follows who is placed in it.
Your group's totems and shouts, blessings and debuffs come from the specs placed there.
The comp's open slots count as filled unless you untick it; your clicks stay on top.

sections.heading: Consumables
lines: New Consumables page (Gear menu): the flask, food, stone or oil and potions for your spec.
Best picks for prog nights on the left, a cheaper pick for farm nights on the right.
The middle says what each one is for, like one flask or two elixirs, never both.
Each pick shows what it does, and a check when your bags hold enough for a night.
Missing ones name their guild crafter; the bag button puts them on your shopping list.
Add prog kit and Add farm kit put everything your bags lack on the list in one click.
Damage specs can Sim the kit: the gear sim gives each pick its DPS with the gear you wear.
With Auctionator, what a night's worth costs. Each spec tab has its own kit.
Click a pick to choose your own in the item picker: flasks, elixirs, food, potions...
Right-click a pick to drop it from the prog or farm kit, or go back to the guide's pick.

sections.heading: Feedback
sections.lead: Send the developer a bug, an idea or a change.
lines: New speech bubble next to What's new: send feedback on a bug, an idea or a change.
Pick Something broke, I have an idea, Change something or I love this, and say it.
It reaches the developer even while offline: whoever is online carries it.
Everyone in the guild sees it and can say me too, so the most asked shows.
Point at it: go to the button or page you mean, right-click it, and it's named.
Or Ctrl+right-click anything in DisasterZone to start from it.
Version, zone, spec and DisasterZone's last Lua error go along with a bug.
Yours shows where each one stands: Sent, Received, Planned, Fixed in 1.3.5.
Officers can answer too: "it's already there, under Settings...".
A pop-up when somebody answers, and when yours is in a release you have.
Lines in this changelog name who asked for them; yours glow.
DisasterZone errors offer to report them (Settings > Notifications turns it off).
Demo mode shows a filled feedback page to try it out.
/dz bug, /dz idea and /dz feedback open the form.
The share icon in the top bar links the Feedback page, or the item you have open.

sections.heading: Guild polls
lines: New Guild > Polls: the GM, officers and Guild Council ask, the people they pick answer.
Ask everyone, teams or lineups, officers, the council, raid leaders, ranks or players.
Four kinds: one answer, several answers, yes or no, and Pick days.
Pick days: tick each night can, if needed or can't; the best night is framed in gold.
Results show live, after you vote or when the poll closes. Names are always shown.
Polls that don't ask you never show up. One answer per player, from any character.
A pop-up when a poll arrives (never in combat): yes or no is answered right there.
The asker sees who hasn't answered and can nudge them, close the poll early or extend it.
Members who were offline get the poll and its answers when they log in.

sections.heading: Crafting materials (Nether Vortex)
lines: A dropped Vortex lists who wants it: the crafts on their lists that use it.
Each craft shows who in the guild makes it, or that nobody does.
Squares show how many each person already has toward their craft.
Whoever it completes a craft for comes first, then whoever is closest.
The roll popup says what it's for: "for Belt of Blasting · you have 1 of 2".
Two crafts on your lists? Click the craft in the popup to pick the one you want.
After the award: the craft it counts toward, and Whisper tells the crafter.

sections.heading: Swing timer (Retribution)
lines: New swing timer for seal twisting, built in: it shows on Retribution Paladins in combat.
The orange zone is when to press Seal of Blood, already moved earlier by your ping.
A red line warns when a GCD pressed now would cost you the twist.
Above the bar: what to press next, and Judgement when it is time for it.
Optional plan lane: the next 7 seconds of the rotation.
It follows WoWSims' Ret rotation and your haste; Exorcism and Consecration are opt-in.
After each fight: twists landed, late and clipped, in Settings and /dz swing report.
/dz swing unlock to move it, /dz swing for your latency and where the numbers come from.

sections.heading: Paladin blessings (Pally Power, built in)
lines: New Blessings planner for every paladin spec: paladins as rows, classes as columns.
Click a cell to pick a blessing, or drag one from the top onto a class or a whole paladin.
Right-click clears, the wheel steps through, Shift-click gives every class the same.
Exceptions: one player gets another blessing, like tanks on Light instead of Salvation.
Click a paladin's aura to set it; a red edge when two in one party run the same.
Live in every cell: who is missing the blessing and when it runs out.
Auto-assign fills it from everyone's talents: Kings first, then the best Might and Wisdom.
Presets save the plan per raid; Report posts who gives what to the raid.
It speaks Pally Power's language, so Pally Power users in the raid share the same plan.
The leader and assistants assign; paladins can let anyone assign them.
New buff bar in groups, in two looks: a rail of class rings or a strip of tiles.
Rings and lines drain as blessings run out; what to do next glows and says when.
Bless a class again and it eases back to calm with a soft golden bloom.
Click a class for what it needs next: its Greater Blessing first, then each exception.
Right-click a class for its players: click one to recast their blessing right away.
Scroll on a player there to give them a single blessing instead.
Pick the look in the planner's More menu or Settings > Class tools.
Set it to Always to keep it solo too: bless yourself with the one your spec wants.
Key binding "Bless next" casts whatever is due. /dz bless opens the planner.

sections.heading: Shaman totems (ShamanPower, built in)
lines: New Totem planner for every shaman spec: a row per shaman, a column per element.
Totems only reach the shaman's party, so each row shows the raid group and who is in it.
Click a totem to pick one (the menu says what each does); right-click clears it.
Twist Windfury with Grace of Air for Enhancement, right in the Air menu.
Earth Shield: pick the tank for each Restoration shaman, with the charges left on them.
Heroism is raid-wide: pick the one shaman who casts it and when, and a backup.
Two shamans set to cast it show in red: Exhaustion wastes the second one.
Groups without a shaman show in red with what they miss; Suggest a swap moves one in.
Or drag a shaman's card onto that row (leader or assistant, out of combat).
Boss tabs: change a totem for one fight only, like resistance totems for Hydross.
A boss can have a second totem for its next phase: it goes on right-click on the bar.
Auto-assign fills it from each party: Windfury and Strength of Earth for melee.
Casters get Wrath of Air and Totem of Wrath.
It speaks ShamanPower's language, so ShamanPower users in the raid share the same plan.
Shamans with no totem addon still get a row: the leader plans for them, Report posts it.
New totem bar in groups, a rail or a strip: rings drain as your totems run out.
Twisting: the Air ring is Windfury on the party's weapons, and says when to drop it again.
A red count on a totem shows party members out of its range; hover it for who.
Click a totem to drop it; right-click drops the other one (twist partner or next phase).
Mana Tide, Earth Shield and Heroism sit on the bar too.
Weapon imbue reminders are a setting, off by default.
/dz totems opens the planner. Demo mode shows it all with a made-up Serpentshrine raid.

sections.heading: Class tools
lines: New Settings > Class tools: everything DisasterZone adds for your class, in one place.
Each tool is a card that opens and closes for its settings; all start closed.
A switch on each card turns that tool on or off.
Demo mode shows every class's tools with a made-up raid, to try them anywhere.

sections.heading: Notifications
lines: New bell left of the sync mark: its gold number counts what waits for your answer.
Click it for what needs you (polls, raids to answer, join requests) and the week's news.
Answer right there (Yes / No, Accept, Review); handled things leave by themselves.
All notifications opens a page with every section, and what you handled this week.
One pop-up look for everything, one at a time, never in combat; Later keeps it.
Counts show on the tabs, in the menus and on the minimap button; its tooltip lists them.
Settings > Notifications: per kind, pop-up, sound or a chat line; quiet for an hour.
Home's chips come from the same list, so Home and the bell always agree.
Several of one kind are one chip on Home ("3 polls waiting"); its tooltip lists them.

sections.heading: A new window frame
lines: Every DisasterZone window has its own frame now, in place of the grey Blizzard one.
The main window's header shows the next raid's art, the seal and the guild's line.
The guild line says who is online and when the next raid starts.
Small windows get a slim strip of that art, the seal, the title and a flat close X.
A soft shadow and a gold glint under the header; nothing inside a window moved.
The window body has a faint stone grain and a soft light under the header.

sections.heading: Raids, Gear and Guild menus
lines: The menus under Raids, Gear and Guild are a spotlight now: the pages on the left.
The page under the mouse shows big on the right, with its art slowly drifting.
Each page shows what is going on: the next raid, items to decide, who is online.
Jump straight into a page's tabs from the menu: Teams, Strategies, Loot log, Recipes.
Gear holds My BiS, Gear sim, Consumables and Atlas; each bar shows only that page's tools.

sections.heading: Cleaner counts
lines: Every count has one new look: the bell, tabs, menus, the minimap button, the waitlist.
A solid gold circle with sharp dark digits, like today on the calendar; no thin ring.
On a tab the count sits right after the name and never bumps into the next tab.

sections.heading: Lighter on memory
lines: The 3D boss rooms moved into a second folder, DisasterZone_Rooms, in the same zip.
They load only when you open a 3D board, the Raid Trainer or chess: about 20 MB less.
Install both folders. The AddOn list shows the rooms as DisasterZone 3D rooms.

sections.heading: Fixes
lines: Guild > Members: share and note icons click again on your own card and offline members'.
The top bar's share icon now works on Polls, Map, Atlas, My Log and Notifications too.

sections.heading: Azeromon is back
lines: Disastercraft is gone: Azeromon, the beast-taming game, is back in Guild > Games.
Played it before? CONTINUE picks up your old save, beasts and badges included.
A /reload in the middle of a scene undoes it: no double gifts, prizes or skipped gates.
Trades can't copy a beast any more, and a slow turn gives only one player the win.
Messages and menus no longer freeze the game when a duel or trade arrives.
The guild board, bounties and Guild Hall trophies count right, and alts only once.
Every fix is listed in the game's own What's new, on its title screen.

changelog.title: A new window frame, gear sim, meters and Azeromon

sections.heading: My Log (opt-in)
sections.lead: Record your own play in every boss pull. Opt-in.
lines: New in Settings > My Log: record your own play in every raid boss pull. Off by default.
Saved on your PC only and never sent: nobody else can see it, the loot council included.
It records damage, healing, shields, damage taken, avoidance, casts, buffs and deaths.
Death recaps keep your last 10 seconds: every hit, heal and cast, with your health.
Heroic dungeon bosses too if you switch that on. /dz mylog last prints your latest pull.
Raids > My Log: each raid night against the one before, with four headline numbers.
A row per boss: your number, the change since your last kill, active time, last 8 kills.
It opens on your role's numbers; Damage, Healing and Tanking are there for everyone.
Click a boss: the fight second by second against another kill, with your idle gaps in red.
Under it, every ability (or what hit you) with its change, avoidable hits marked.
Deaths: what killed you most, and the last 10 seconds of each death with your health.
The boss's side is logged too: its casts, its shields and phases, yells, adds dying.
Timeline (on a boss): every cast you made, lane by lane, under the boss's own lane.
Idle gaps show red across the lanes. Hover for what happened; scroll to zoom in.
Demo mode fills My Log with made-up raid nights, so you can look around first.

sections.heading: Games, in the spotlight
lines: Guild > Games opens on a spotlight: one game's poster in front, the others at its sides.
Turn it with the arrows, the mouse wheel or the dots, or click a poster at the side.
The posters are alive: your Bingo card fills in as the raid goes.
Raid Trainer's poster lists its bosses with your best clear time for each.
Each poster shows a result of yours and who in the guild is playing it right now.
During a raid's Bingo game the tab opens on Bingo, LIVE, saying how close your card is.
Opening a game: the poster grows and darkens into its backdrop, then the game rises in.
< GAMES at the top goes back the same way: the painting shrinks back into its place.
Council Bingo, redrawn: a header with the raid's painting, LIVE, your lines and squares.
The card fills the page: calm squares with the icon over the words.
Rare and legendary squares wear their colour like item quality; legendary ones shimmer.
Marked squares take your dauber's ink and its marker; completed lines turn gold.
The race, the latest squares and the season sit beside the card, your dauber under them.

sections.heading: Karazhan Chess
sections.lead: Chess on Medivh's own board, in 3D.
lines: New game in Guild > Games: chess on Medivh's own board in the Gamesman's Hall, in 3D.
The pieces are the event's creatures at their real sizes; the Echo of Medivh looks on.
Pieces walk to their square; a capture is a blow and a fall. Right-drag turns the camera.
While you play the board fills the page: only a light layer over it, the moves on request.
Play the Echo of Medivh as Apprentice, Magus or Guardian, Alliance or Horde.
He speaks his own lines from the event when pieces fall, and when he cheats.
Medivh cheats (switch it off if you like): fire under your pieces, a hand on his.
Fire burns under up to 3 of your pieces: move them out within 2 moves or they burn.
Hand of Medivh: up to 4 of his pieces may also step one square any way for 4 moves.
Or he mends his army: the last piece you took from him returns to the board.
His cheats never check you, never touch a king and always leave you a move.
Challenge a guild member: one move at a time, whenever you are both online.
A move made while they're offline reaches them when they log in. Resign or offer a draw.
Guild ladder: results of guild games go round the guild; everyone sees the same ratings.
A flat board too (before a client restart, or picked over the board).
Its poster is the hall in 3D, mid-fight, and says how many games wait for your move.
/dz chess opens it.

sections.heading: Teams, redesigned
sections.lead: Every team as a banner, its lineups as tabs.
lines: Raids > Teams opens on a board: every team as a banner, yours first, with its next raid.
Each team has a theme: pick the raid whose painting is its banner (... > Theme).
A team's lineups are tabs on its banner, each with how full it is.
Groups and Comp are one switch; the actions for each sit on the same row.
Players are cards like raid frames: spec icon, name, and the spec under it.
Empty seats are real drop spots as big as a card; the dragged card follows the cursor.
A label under the dragged card says where it lands, or who it swaps with.
With a target comp, its open slots wait in the empty seats: the spec, who could fill it.
Each group's title shows the party buffs it gets; drag it onto another group to swap them.
Unassigned players are cards under the groups (Kara lineups: beside the two groups).
The raid buffs sit next to Groups | Comp; unsaved changes are said on the banner.
Comp: a band per role with the same cards, five a row, and a pip per slot.
Comp: drag a player onto an open slot to fill it; they take its spec and its seat.
Comp: drag a slot's player to Unassigned to take them out of the groups.
Switching Groups and Comp slides the switch and glides the new view in.
The waitlist is an icon at the end of the lineup tabs, with a badge counting who waits.
Click it for the line: drag a player straight into a group, or join and leave it there.
Bloodlust / Heroism counts as a raid buff (raid-wide on these realms), not a group one.

sections.heading: Upcoming raids in the same look
lines: Raids > Upcoming: each raid is a banner of its painting, the date in gold when it's close.
Each banner has your answer (or Accept / Tentative), who accepted by role and a fill bar.
A raid's page has the Teams banner: date, name, where and who; the raid's note under them.
Your answer is one switch on the banner, with your spec, character and note under it.
Sign-ups, Groups and Assignments are tabs on the banner, each with how far along it is.
Raid leader, Edit, Cancel and Delete sit in the banner's ... menu; Share is the top icon.
Sign-ups: a band per role with players as cards, five a row; requests to join on top.
Approve or deny a request right on its card. Bench, absent and unanswered are bands below.
Tentative players fade and show a ?, a note shows its icon, guests say Guest.
Groups: the Teams groups (cards, empty seats, party buffs, drag a group's title to swap).
A raid locked to a team with a target comp shows its open slots in the empty seats.
Assignments: each boss is a card with its picture, strategy and how many slots are filled.
A strategy that still has to be picked shows in orange; a boss without one offers Create.
Each boss's strategy menu ends with No strategy: the raid goes without one for that boss.

sections.heading: Guild > Map (new)
lines: See where guildmates are, on the game's own maps, fully explored. Opt-in: share to see.
Share your exact spot or only your zone; sharing your zone shows everyone by zone.
Always hidden in battlegrounds and arenas. The eye at the top right changes it.
Tabs per continent with how many are there. Click a region to open its map.
Right-click or the path at the top goes back out. The list beside it goes by zone.
Crowds are rings in their class colours; dungeons and raids sit at their entrance.
A white skull marks a dungeon, a gold one a raid.
Dots glide as people move; your arrow follows you and turns with you.
Right-click someone to whisper or invite them; click for their Members profile.
Members: the card says where they are, or the zone they were last seen in.
The game's world map (M) shows the same dots (... menu on the Map page).
Demo mode shows a crowded made-up guild on the map, no sharing needed.

sections.heading: Menus
lines: The Raids, Gear and Guild menus show each page with a line saying what it holds.
The page you're on has a gold bar; Events wears its BETA pill in the menu too.

sections.heading: Raids: fixes
lines: Two officers saving the same team at once: both changes are kept, not only the later one.
The blacklist no longer loses players when an officer who missed a change edits it.
Deleted raids and teams no longer come back when someone returns after a month away.
A raid's lineup deleted or resized: the whole team counts for it, not another lineup.
A raid locked to teams that were all deleted is open to everyone, not shut to all.
Saved groups follow your answer: Absent takes you out, another character takes your seat.
Invite & sort skips players who answered Absent after the groups were saved.
Raid invites from someone with a dungeon run listed show the game's own invite.
Passing the lead to someone without DisasterZone no longer ends the raid session.
Invite & sort keeps going while the lead passes, and says so when the raid ends.
Missed the end of a raid? Your log ends it when you left, not when you came back.
Names typed in any case are the right player: "rita" on the blacklist blocks Rita.
Every week: each week moves to the day and time you pick, also across a clock change.
Every week can't move raids by a week or more: cancel a week to skip it.

changelog.title: My Log, Teams and Karazhan Chess

sections.heading: A shorter header
lines: The header has five tabs now: Home, Raids, Gear, Dungeons and Guild, for everyone.
Raids holds Raids and Council; Gear: My BiS and Atlas; Guild: Members, Events, Games.
Hover Raids, Gear or Guild to see its pages; click it for the one you used last.
Every page is the same as before, only where you find it changed.
Tooltips get the flat look of the dropdowns and fade in the same way.
Smoother page switching: pages load in the background and fade in; faster to open.

sections.heading: Minimap button
lines: A new look: the DisasterZone seal instead of the blue bag, also in the AddOns list.
Left-click it and your pinned sections fan out around it; click one to go straight there.
The + at the end of the arc picks your pins (up to 6); right-click a pin to move it.
Pins are shared by all your characters. Right-click the button to open the window.
A new DisasterZone page in Options > AddOns: open any section, or right-click to pin it.
Its banner: your next raid's painting with embers, a countdown, who's online, your BiS.

sections.heading: Events
sections.lead: The guild's own events: duel cups, races, contests.
lines: A new tab, Events: the guild's own events, like duel cups, races, hunts and contests.
It wears a small BETA tag for now: still being tested, so things may change or break.
Build one in the event builder: snap pieces together like a puzzle, no code.
Start from one of 8 examples: a duel cup, hide and seek, a mount race, a fishing derby...
Stages run along the top (Sign-up, Matches, Finals, Prizes); Always runs in each of them.
A few blocks build any event: tags (Hiders, Out), scores (Fish, Time), places, lists.
Places: stand on the spot and click Set, or pick it on the map.
Ask questions (votes, quizzes, judges' scores 1 to 10) and give players buttons (Hint).
One piece hears the game: a duel won, a kill, a fish caught, loot, a death, mounting.
Hide and seek: a seeker clicks a hider up close; a /target macro doesn't count.
Smart blocks do the big jobs: Sign-up, and Matches (elimination or round robin, best of).
Matches are won by a duel, or by your own pieces: a fishing duel, a quiz duel.
Open a smart block to see the pieces it's made of; make your own copy to change it.
Click a blank to pick what fits there, or drag a piece into it.
The addon tells players itself: banners on screen, lines in the tracker, prompts.
Guild chat only gets what you post there yourself, like the champion's name.
Practice first: your event runs with 16 dummies, and nothing is sent or saved.
Duels count by themselves: the game says who won, and nobody has to click a thing.
If the two players disagree, the event asks them, then the host decides.
Host it on a day and a place: it shows on the Home calendar with a purple dot.
The live board draws itself from the event: the bracket, scores, teams, the map, a race.
The host gets controls; if the host goes offline, another player takes over the event.
Under the minimap: when you're up, your team and score, an arrow to where you're going.
Signed up? From 30 min before, the tracker points you to where the event meets.
Every map shows you, the zone and each place; click a place to be shown the way.
If the host reloads or someone takes over, a quiz, a vote or a Hint goes on where it was.
Ranked events count for the season: points, badges and titles.
The GM, officers and guild council rank events; send yours in for a review.
They can also remove any event from the calendar or library, and clear the review lists.
Your title shows on your tooltip, with your place in the season.
Share an event in chat: the link opens its page, or the event in the builder.

sections.heading: Dungeons
lines: A run's leader invites you: one pop-up, the run's own, no longer under Blizzard's.
Asked to join and the leader accepts? You join straight away: your Join was the answer.
Pass the party lead and the run goes with it, with everyone who asked to join.
Your run in Blizzard's Group Finder: click the eye on it (it looks around while listed).
Or switch Pugs on when you list a run: it goes into the Group Finder with the same click.
Players looking for that dungeon in the Group Finder show up on your run, roles and level.
Anyone who whispers you while you're listed shows up too, with what they wrote.
Invite, whisper or set aside each one; a pug joins as the open role they fit.
A run for later with Pugs on: a pop-up when it starts asks to list it in the Group Finder.
Its note is yours to type in Blizzard's window (addons can't): ... > Note opens it.
A run that ends by itself while listed there asks you to take the listing down.
Editing a listed run keeps the Group Finder in step (new dungeon, or later: taken out).
Your run: click someone's place to set their role (pugs who whispered you start as DPS).
The leader leaving the party leaves the run with it: the new leader runs it.
Saying no to a run's invite takes back your ask; a failed invite can be sent again.
In a group? No Join and no pings (no invite can reach you); leaders see you as in a group.
Asks are forgotten after 20 minutes on both sides; after a no, you may ask again in 10.
Pugs show their class on everyone's board; whispers with item links read cleanly.

sections.heading: Raids: team lineups and waitlists
sections.lead: One roster, many lineups, and a waitlist.
lines: A team keeps one roster and any number of lineups: e.g. two 25s and three Kara 10s.
Each lineup has its own groups, specs and target comp: pick one with the chips.
+ Lineup adds a 10- or 25-man one; click the open one's chip to rename, copy or delete.
Not in a group is now Unassigned: on the roster, but not counted for the comp or buffs.
Waitlist: not on the roster, waiting for a spot. Join or leave it yourself on Teams.
Waitlisted players aren't invited to the team's raids and don't count for the comp.
Organizers move waitlisted players up or down, or drag them into a group to take them in.
A raid uses the team's lineup of its size; New raid > Teams picks one when there are more.
It invites that lineup's players (in its groups); a team without one invites its roster.
Who could fill an open spot lists Unassigned and the waitlist first.
Fixed: Add members on the Teams page opened its list behind the window.

sections.heading: Raids: New raid, redone; several raids in one
lines: New raid opens over the Raids tab: raid tiles, a date strip, a live preview of the card.
Pick several raids for one night (Gruul + Mag): the order you click is the night's.
One sign-up, one set of groups and one comp for the whole night; mixed sizes allowed.
No size to pick: the raids you pick say it (the larger one wins).
When: a week of days (a dot where a raid is planned), the calendar for later, the time.
The calendar button drops a flat month calendar, with the same arrows as the rest.
Who: one search for teams and players; the teams on these raids lately come first.
Picks show as chips (teams in gold, with how many they invite); click one to drop it.
Any number of teams fits: the Who row stays two lines, the rest goes into "+3 more".
A raid for many teams names as many as fit on its card, then how many more.
Sign-ups: Everyone, Teams + invited or Private, in one choice.
Strategies and Assignments list every boss of the night, in order.
The board's raid filter finds a raid of several under each of them.

sections.heading: Raids: Guests, redone
lines: Guest book: now a view of the Raids tab, Raids > Guests (GM, officers, raid leaders).
Pick a player: their page shows their last raid's art, raids, boss kills and no-shows.
Their raids, next one first: the kills they were there for, bench, raids they missed.
The loot council also sees the items they received there.
Recruit and Add to a raid are on their page; a check marks raids they have a seat on.
Click the note (or the pencil) to change it right there; Enter saves, Escape undoes.
Type a name in the search box to add a player who hasn't raided with you yet.
Give a new player a class (and spec) as you add them: they can go straight into a raid.
The blacklist is a filter of the same list; type a name there to blacklist a player.
Right-click a player in the list for the quick actions.
Remove takes a player out of the book; they come back if they raid with you again.

sections.heading: Switches
lines: Every on / off switch now moves: the knob slides over and the green follows it.

sections.heading: Dropdowns and menus
lines: Every dropdown and right-click menu has the calendar's look: dark, flat, gold accents.
They drop in: a quick fade as they slide into place; submenus slide out to the side.
A dropdown's list opens right under it, and the dropdown lights up gold while it's open.
Check boxes and choices look like the invite list's; titles are gold, lines are thin.
Click the dropdown again, click elsewhere or press Escape to close it.
Tooltips no longer cover an open menu: they move to a free side, or hide if there is none.

sections.heading: Buttons
lines: Every button has a finer finish: a soft light at the top, a deeper fill, softer corners.
Gold buttons are a richer gold with a quieter edge that lights up when you point at them.
Pointing at a button eases it in, and a soft light sweeps across it once.
Pressing dips it, letting go flashes it; picking an option fades the choice across.
Tabs: the gold underline grows out from the middle; pointing at a tab shows a faint one.

sections.heading: Text fields
lines: A name too long for its field shows its start with "..." after you click away.
Point at a cut-off name to read it in full.

sections.heading: Atlas: costs and your currencies
lines: Items a vendor sells show their cost with icons: Honor, Arena Points, Badges, marks.
A cost is red while you hold less than it asks, white once you can buy it.
A bar at the bottom shows your Honor, Arena Points, Badges and what the page pays with.
Point at an item: its currencies light up and the bar says how many you lack or keep.
The tooltip lists each part of the cost: what you have, how many more you need.
Badges and marks in your bank count too; the bar reminds you to take them out first.
Arena and honor sets show what the set costs, or what is left once you own pieces.
Prices are your realm's own: every vendor you open teaches the addon its prices.

sections.heading: My BiS: gems and enchants
sections.lead: Sockets, gems and enchants on your BiS picks.
lines: Every pick shows its sockets and enchant as small icons next to where it drops.
Click them to choose: each socket in its colour, the socket bonus, and the enchant.
Suggestions use WoWSims' gems and enchants for your spec, ranked by its stat weights.
A unique gem goes in once; a gem only skips the socket bonus when it's worth more.
Suggest > Fill empty sockets and enchants does the whole phase; what you chose stays.
Search in the gem list finds any other gem.
Under the obtained count: how many gems and enchants are still to choose.
... > Shopping puts the phase's crafted picks, gems and enchants on your shopping list.
Hover a pick: its tooltip shows the item with your gems and enchant.
Imports from Sixty Upgrades, WoWSims and Wowhead keep gems and enchants; exports too.
The council sees your gems and enchants on your list too.

sections.heading: Fixes
lines: Item names no longer get stuck on "Loading..." until you switch views.

changelog.title: Events, the Group Finder, gems and enchants

sections.heading: Dungeons: the guild's own LFG
sections.lead: List a 5-man run or join one, inside the guild.
lines: New Dungeons tab: list a 5-man run or join one, all inside the guild.
I'm up for a run: the guild sees you're free, and you get a ping when a run needs you.
Every run shows its open places; the one that wants your role glows. Join asks the leader.
Your run: Accept sends the invite. Guildies who are free and fit show up to invite.
Cards say what stops you (heroic key, lockout, level) or what drops your BiS there.
List a run: pick a dungeon, now or later, add a note; the preview is what the guild sees.
A star on a dungeon: online guildies with BiS there. DAILY: your daily quest for it.
Share your run in chat with the share icon; later runs show on the Home calendar.

sections.heading: Raids, redesigned
sections.lead: Every raid as a card: answer right on it.
lines: Upcoming: every raid is a card with its loading screen; answer right on the card.
A raid's page: a banner with the facts and your answer, then its tabs.
Your spec, character and note sit under your answer; the raid's note under the banner.
Sign-ups: four role columns with spec icons; bench, absent and no response below.
Groups: the five parties side by side, their buffs at the bottom, the raid's on top.
Drag a player: their card follows the mouse and the spot it lands on lights up.
Strategies: raids as art strips, strategy cards with Edit and a More menu.
Strategy board: a cleaner header, page tabs, a one-row toolbar, flat job cards.
Names, page names and notes are typed in place; Discard and Delete page ask first.
Assigning keeps the map full size: the raid's players sit above the tables, by role.
Raid log: raid cards, a banner, a Linked to picker, who came, and tabs.
Teams redone: team chips, a team card with its next raids, the raid page's groups.
Teams ask before unsaved changes are lost; Copy, Clear groups, Add several, spec by icon.
Teams draft a target comp: open spots show on the team card and in raid Sign-ups.
Comp tab: start from a preset, steppers per role, bench, LF message for the chat box.
Ranged players have their own role icon, a bow, so melee and ranged read apart.

sections.heading: My BiS and Home
lines: My BiS: a Pre-raid list before P1 (dungeons, reputation, crafting, badges), just for you.
My BiS: phases as tabs, your gear around the model, what's still to get under it.
Home: a calmer calendar: today in gold, only the month's weeks, nothing cut off.
Home: the line under the next raid only shows what's missing.
Home: the banner slides through this week's raids; the bars or arrows pick one.

sections.heading: A new look everywhere
lines: The sync mark in the top bar turns while your list is shared, then draws a green check.
Atlas: loading-screen banners, item icons and a star count of your BiS picks per boss.
Atlas: hover an item and click + to add it to your BiS list.
Settings: sections in a side menu; every option a switch or a dropdown, explained.
Council roster: every BiS pick shows its icon; filter by class and role with one click.
Council items: raids with their art, who wants what as name chips, unwanted items folded.

sections.heading: Ask to join a locked raid
sections.lead: See locked raids and ask to join them.
lines: Raids locked to a team are now listed for the whole guild, with their roster.
Outside the team? Pick an answer to ask to join; your note goes with it.
Who runs the raid sees Requests to join under the roster: click a name to approve or deny.
Approved: invited to that raid only, and you see its strategies. Absent takes it back.
Private (raid editor): the old way, hidden from the rest and no requests.

sections.heading: Loot council panel
lines: Once an item is awarded its rolls fold away; Show rolls at the top right opens them again.
Boss drop panel: item cards with BiS/Alt/OS tags, one gold Award, the rest in a menu.
Roll popup, BiS toast and raid bar restyled; raid options sit behind a gear icon.

sections.heading: Strategy boards: encounter objects
lines: New strategies start with the fight's objects and helpers where the game puts them.
Vashj's generators, Magtheridon's cubes and channelers, Kil'jaeden's orbs and more.
Akama's channelers, Leotheras' spellbinders, Zul'jin's spirits, Netherspite's portals.
Right-click one, State: Active, Channelling, Dead...; selected ones switch together.
Beams show on the map and in 3D, with the spell's own effect where the game has one.
Icon > Encounter objects: a phase's spawns at their spots, like Kael's weapons.
Routes and areas: Jan'alai's hatchers and bombs, Felmyst's lanes, Aran's Blizzard.
Icon > From a model ID: place any creature or game object by NPC, object or display ID.
A Wowhead link works as well; the creature comes at the size the game draws it.
Strategies with these reach members once they run 1.3.1.

sections.heading: Walking in 3D
lines: The walk button has its own icon: a figure striding over a ring.
Drag it into the room: a ring on the floor and a see-through you show where you will land.
The ring turns red where there is nothing to stand on, and letting go there does nothing.

sections.heading: Crafting materials
lines: Hold Shift over anything crafted: its materials, and how many you have in bags and bank.
In Atlas and Members, Shift + mouse wheel sets how many to make; the materials add up.
Shift + click breaks them down a step (bolts into cloth); Shift + right-click goes back.
Atlas: Spellcloth, Shadowcloth and Primal Mooncloth are items again, with their icons.

sections.heading: Atlas: shopping list
lines: Hover a craft in the Atlas or Members and click its bag; Shift sets how many first.
Your list sits at the top of the Atlas, grouped by who makes it: most of it first.
Materials add up with what's in your bags and bank; the missing ones come first.
Pick a crafter for their part of the list; Whisper types the ask with the links.
With Auctionator, one line says what the missing materials cost at the auction house.

sections.heading: Members
lines: The roster lists online players first, then away, then offline; the highest level first.
A member's Characters card lists their raid teams: click one to open it in the Raids tab.
Hovering a member shows their team too.
A calmer roster with class circles, skill levels and a profession filter.
Member card: spec chips, the officer note under them, recipes fold out under professions.

sections.heading: Fixes
lines: Someone walking in the room no longer makes a boss vanish or shows up white and jittering.
Nightbane's 3D room is the Master's Terrace again, not the chess hall and tower rooms.
Walking in a 3D room moves like the Raid Trainer: smooth strafing, mouse look and steps.
Magtheridon no longer has squares cut out of him in the 3D room.
Bosses in 3D stand on their spot: the Lurker and others were yards off their circle.
Karazhan and Sunwell 3D rooms show the right textures; many surfaces had the wrong one.
Prince Malchezaar's 3D room now shows his platform, not a floor far below it.

changelog.title: Dungeons tab, ask to join locked raids
